codeReview.summary: The new AgentRuntime class (lines 554–657 of runtime.py) correctly satisfies all four validation assertions. It holds interpreter, history, tools, and core_memory as instance attributes; calls discover_tools() during __init__ and passes the tool list to FleetAgent; accumulates dspy.History across turns in chat_turn(); and exposes core memory via get_core_memory(), get_core_memory_key(), and set_core_memory_key(). Code is clean, well-typed, well-docstringed, and follows project conventions. All 30 tests pass (0.16s, no failures).

issues.description: The module docstring correctly notes that _LegacyAgentRuntime is 'to be deleted', but it still exists and is large (~530 lines). No cleanup ticket or deprecation guard is present. This is pre-existing technical debt, not introduced by this feature, but worth tracking.

core_memory is exposed as a plain mutable dict. Tools that hold a reference to it (via get_core_memory()) can mutate it directly without going through set_core_memory_key(). This is intentional per VAL-AGENT-010 ('core memory accessible by tool functions'), but a comment or design note clarifying this is intentional would help future maintainers.

test_max_iters_forwarded_to_agent accesses rt.agent.react._max_iters directly, coupling the test to the internal structure of FleetAgent. If FleetAgent's internal attribute name changes the test breaks silently. A public accessor or a less brittle assertion (e.g. check that FleetAgent was called with max_iters=25 via mock) would be more robust, but this is a test quality concern, not a blocking defect.

nonBlockingIssues: Legacy _LegacyAgentRuntime still present with no deprecation guard (~530 lines of dead weight)
core_memory dict is directly mutable by reference — intentional but undocumented
Test couples to internal FleetAgent attribute name (agent.react._max_iters)

sharedStateObservations.observation: The module keeps the large _LegacyAgentRuntime class alongside the new AgentRuntime with a 'to be deleted' note in the docstring, but no deprecation decorator, no TODO comment with a ticket number, and no mention in AGENTS.md. AGENTS.md says 'do not reference the removed runtime/models/rlm_runtime_modules.py', implying similar cleanup is expected elsewhere, but the pattern for how legacy code is flagged/tracked before deletion is undocumented.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/fleet_rlm/runtime/agent/runtime.py lines 1-7 (module docstring) and lines 36-540 (_LegacyAgentRuntime body). AGENTS.md src/fleet_rlm/AGENTS.md has no guidance on deprecation tagging.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The new AgentRuntime accepts and holds an arbitrary interpreter: Any | None but does not use it in chat_turn() or any other method. This matches the feature spec (manages the interpreter as a held reference) but callers have no way to interact with the interpreter through AgentRuntime's public API. If future features need to pass the interpreter to tools, a pattern for exposing it will need to be established.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/fleet_rlm/runtime/agent/runtime.py lines 566-567: self.interpreter is assigned and lines 606-630: chat_turn() does not reference self.interpreter at all.

summary: PASS. AgentRuntime correctly satisfies VAL-AGENT-007 through VAL-AGENT-010: it holds all required state (agent, interpreter, history, tools, core_memory), discovers and passes tools at init, accumulates history across turns, and exposes core memory via get/set accessors. All 30 unit tests pass. Three non-blocking code quality observations noted (legacy class cleanup, intentionally mutable dict reference, internal attribute coupling in one test). No blocking issues.
